newsitem.title: USA: NHL-QUENNEVILLE NAMED NEW HEAD COACH OF ST LOUIS BLUES.
newsitem.headline: NHL-QUENNEVILLE NAMED NEW HEAD COACH OF ST LOUIS BLUES.

text.p: Joel Quenneville, who resigned Sunday as assistant coach of the Colorado Avalanche, was named the new head coach of the St. Louis Blues on Monday.
The Blues also announced that Ron Caron will remain as the team's general manager through the 1997-98 season.
Quenneville, 38, was in his third season as an assistant with the Avalanche franchise. He had served as head coach of the American Hockey League's Springfield Falcons in 1993-94.

"I'm looking forward to the challenge," said Quenneville. "The decision of leaving Colorado was something to weigh, but this is a great hockey town. After six years of constantly moving from place to place, me and my family are looking forward to settling down here."
The Blues fired head coach-general manager Mike Keenan on December 19 and promoted assistant Jim Roberts to succeed him on an interim basis.
Roberts will return to his duties as associate coach and and Roger Nielsen will remain with the club as an associate.
The Blues were 3-3-3 under Roberts and are 18-20-4 for the season.

Quenneville played in 803 NHL games from 1978-91 for Toronto, the Colorado Rockies, New Jersey, Hartford and Washington, totalling 54 goals and 136 assists. The former defenceman helped lead the Whalers to their only divisional title in 1986-87.
Quenneville will make his debut Tuesday night when the Blues host the Edmonton Oilers.
